newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil retains strength, LSFO looking tight.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil retains strength, LSFO looking tight.

text.p: NWE fuel oil retained its firm tone on Friday with prices steady or a touch firmer.

High sulphur cracked barges gained $2 with trades at $121.50 to $122 fob ARA on the back of improved bunker interest, some problems for prompt loading barrels and December strength filtering into the prompt market.
Cargo prices were steady around $120 cif NWE amid slack activity. Supplies were seen as tightish, but good avails of Russian straight run have been limiting significant gains.
Cracked low sulphur is tighter with a 40-50,000 tonne cargo selling into Italy on Thursday at a p+c quotes related price.
Only one 22-25,000 tonne cargo looks available ex-France for first half December. "It's not until the second half that the bigger (45-50kt) Scandinavia cargo comes up," said one trader.

The low sulphur straight run market was quiet with the U.S on holiday. One buyer was understood to be looking for material following delays with their West African cargo, but with two sellers there was little potential for higher prices. Offers were pegged around $145 fob NWE with the bid close to $141 fob. High sulphur straight run was still available.
